items.title: Complete Fourier-block spectrum of the area-normalized Dirichlet Hessian at a regular polygon
items.work_key: doi:10.5802/jep.250@Journal de l’École polytechnique — Mathématiques 11 (2024), publisher version, DOI 10.5802/jep.250

items.difficulty_reason: Beyond the known block-circulant transform and the existing general shape Hessian, the author uses the symmetric triangular support to evaluate and cancel the area and eigenfunction-gradient terms mode by mode, then uses rotation and parity of the normalized material derivatives to identify the imaginary off-diagonal coefficient. The spectrum depends on that PDE and geometry calculation, rather than the quadratic formula alone.
source_caveats: Published physical p.39, printed p.56, Eq. (4.7) prints B_yy. The second moments and M^3_{n−1} on that page already give A_yy.

Published physical p.40, printed p.57, the first scaled M^3_0 display prints A_xy as the second diagonal entry. The preceding original definition and the following Fourier expansion both display A_yy there.

Published physical p.40, printed p.57, (4.8) repeats A_xy. Both scalar relations needed for the addition of the Fourier blocks are actually printed, immediately before (4.8). The relevant integral is explicit in the later printed p.61 criticality calculation.

The first-row description at physical p.39 includes the Fourier phase in its display; p.38 gives the real block-circulant Hessian and (4.4) applies the phase in the Fourier transform. In the displayed product M^1_j R_{jθ} on p.40 the common −2|P_n| is suppressed locally. The definition on p.39 and the proof of Theorem 4.9 on p.41 both print the factor.

dedup.scope: The public SQL with the exact DOI and nearby polygon Hessian titles returns only 2237. It selects Theorem 3.18 and its Section 3 stability proof, not the fixed-polygon spectrum computation in Section 4. A general block-circulant method does not supply the selected PDE coefficients.
